concepts.title: Three transforms for a two-joint arm
concepts.description: The first transform has zero translation, the second has x1 offset L1, and the third has identity rotation with x2 offset L2.
concepts.subtopic: Three transforms for a two-joint arm

concepts.title: Interpreting the frame diagram
concepts.description: The frame3 origin is at the tip and frame2 at the elbow; identity rotation in T23 means aligned axes.

concepts.title: Checking the general transform entry
concepts.description: Multiplying row3 of Rx by column2 of Rz gives sinα_(i−1)cosθ_i; the printed entry omits both the proper index and cosθ_i factor.

concepts.title: Angular propagation on parallel axes
concepts.description: A rotation about z leaves a z-directed vector unchanged; the revolute relative rate is then added.

concepts.title: Rotation without origin translation
concepts.description: An origin on the fixed joint axis can have zero linear velocity while its attached frame rotates.

concepts.title: Velocity caused by the first-link offset
concepts.description: The source obtains v2=[L1q1dot sinθ2,L1q1dot cosθ2,0], giving (1,√3,0).
concepts.subtopic: Velocity caused by the first-link offset

concepts.title: Consistent frames in velocity propagation
concepts.description: The bracket is expressed in frame i; premultiplying by the rotation into i+1 changes all components to frame i+1, as the worked v2² shows.

concepts.title: Two points on one rigid link
concepts.description: Rigid-body angular velocity is common, whereas an offset point acquires the tangential velocity ω×p.
concepts.subtopic: Two points on one rigid link

concepts.title: Combining inherited and offset velocities
concepts.description: The x component is2; the y component is0+(1−0.5)×1=0.5.

concepts.title: Expressing tip velocity in the base
concepts.description: The two z rotations compose by angle addition, while T23 contributes identity rotation.
concepts.subtopic: Expressing tip velocity in the base

concepts.title: Extracting the planar body Jacobian
concepts.description: Collecting coefficients of the two joint rates produces the displayed2×2 matrix.

concepts.title: Why the task Jacobian has two rows
concepts.description: The slide projects the translational velocity onto the active planar x/y coordinates; it is not claiming a full six-component twist map.
concepts.subtopic: Why the task Jacobian has two rows

concepts.title: Interpreting the second body-Jacobian column
concepts.description: The second joint rotates the tip about the elbow, producing motion perpendicular to the second link.

concepts.title: Changing the Jacobian expression frame
concepts.description: Changing the output-coordinate basis multiplies the velocity map on the left.

concepts.title: Meaning of singularity
concepts.description: Rank loss reduces the instantaneous image of J; it does not erase all joint motion or imply global immobility.

concepts.title: Scope of the determinant test
concepts.description: The determinant shorthand applies to square matrices; rank expresses the more general loss of task directions.

concepts.title: Stretched and folded configurations
concepts.description: det J=L1L2 sinθ2 vanishes when the two links are collinear.

concepts.title: Motion direction in the straight-arm diagram
concepts.description: The base Jacobian has zero first row and second row[L1+L2,L2], so its image is the Y direction.
concepts.subtopic: Motion direction in the straight-arm diagram

concepts.title: Equal-link folded special case
concepts.description: The first column vanishes when equal links fold to the base, but moving the elbow joint alone still gives a nonzero tangential tip velocity.

concepts.title: Inverse Jacobian for a Cartesian command
concepts.description: J⁰=[[-1,−1],[1,0]], so vy=q1dot=0 and vx=−q2dot=1.
concepts.subtopic: Inverse Jacobian for a Cartesian command

concepts.title: Rate growth on a horizontal approach
concepts.description: cos(θ2/2) tends to1 while sinθ2 tends to0; q1dot is their positive ratio and q2dot is minus twice that ratio.
concepts.subtopic: Rate growth on a horizontal approach

concepts.title: Why not every near-singular command diverges
concepts.description: cos(π/2+θ2)=−sinθ2 and cos(π/2)=0 cancel the apparent singular denominator for this tangential command.
concepts.subtopic: Why not every near-singular command diverges

concepts.title: Static-equilibrium procedure
concepts.description: Static equilibrium is determined from force and moment balance, then the actuator component along the joint freedom is extracted.

concepts.title: Assumptions of the static example
concepts.description: The source excludes link weight while retaining the end load and transmitted force/moment balances.

concepts.title: Meaning of the neighboring-link force
concepts.description: The neighboring-link action/reaction pair has opposite directions; coordinate conversion is a separate operation.

concepts.title: Direction of static-load propagation
concepts.description: The distal load supplies boundary data; each preceding link adds the transmitted and offset moment.

concepts.title: Why moment propagation needs a cross product
concepts.description: A force at an offset contributes the vector moment r×f about the chosen origin.
concepts.subtopic: Why moment propagation needs a cross product

concepts.title: Calculating the transmitted moment
concepts.description: p×f contributes+2 N·m about z, which adds to the existing+1 N·m couple.

concepts.title: Coordinates before adding moments
concepts.description: Vector components must use one basis before vector addition; moment magnitude alone loses direction.

concepts.title: Origin shift of a pure couple
concepts.description: The translation term is p×f, so a pure couple with f=0 is independent of origin, though its coordinates rotate.
concepts.subtopic: Origin shift of a pure couple

concepts.title: Revolute and prismatic actuator efforts
concepts.description: Each actuator supplies the scalar component conjugate to its one allowed motion: axis moment for rotation, axis force for translation.

concepts.title: Positive joint effort
concepts.description: The sign is tied to the selected positive generalized coordinate, not a universal room direction or magnitude.

concepts.title: Why the distal torque depends on f_y
concepts.description: The offset is L2 along x2, and frames2/3 are aligned; only the transverse y force creates a z moment about joint2.
concepts.subtopic: Why the distal torque depends on f_y

concepts.title: Rotating the force toward the base
concepts.description: Rz(90°) maps(x,y) to(−y,x).
concepts.subtopic: Rotating the force toward the base

concepts.title: Force mapping versus velocity mapping
concepts.description: Virtual work yields a transpose, not an inverse; the planar example’s torque matrix equals J³ transposed.

concepts.title: Matching a force with its Jacobian
concepts.description: The Jacobian’s output coordinates and the force components must refer to the same task basis and point.
concepts.subtopic: Matching a force with its Jacobian

concepts.title: A nonzero force can require zero actuator torque
concepts.description: The radial force has zero moment about both joint axes in this ideal geometry; structural stresses and load limits remain separate.
concepts.subtopic: A nonzero force can require zero actuator torque

concepts.title: Adding a terminal moment
concepts.description: A pure z couple propagates unchanged through planar z rotations and acts about both revolute axes.

concepts.title: Work of a transverse force
concepts.description: Work uses F·δx=|F||δx|cosφ, not the magnitude product alone.

concepts.title: Scalar virtual work
concepts.description: A force-displacement dot product is scalar work, with dimensions N·m=J.

concepts.title: Why the transpose appears
concepts.description: For independent joint coordinates, equality of the linear forms for arbitrary δq identifies their coefficients.

concepts.title: Generalizing the six-joint notation
concepts.description: The task wrench has six components, while each joint contributes one generalized effort and one Jacobian column.

concepts.title: Transpose mapping for a redundant task map
concepts.description: Each joint effort is the dot product of its Jacobian column with F.
concepts.subtopic: Transpose mapping for a redundant task map

concepts.title: Checking task and joint power
concepts.description: v=Jqdot=(0.5,0.1), giving F·v=1.5+0.4=1.9 W; τ=(3,8,7) gives the same joint power.

concepts.title: Applied wrench versus environmental reaction
concepts.description: The lecture’s positive applied-hand wrench is opposite to the environment’s reaction; static generalized force balance is τ_act+JᵀF_ext=0.

concepts.title: Order of Cartesian velocity and force components
concepts.description: The lecture places three linear components before three angular components, and force before moment.
concepts.subtopic: Order of Cartesian velocity and force components

concepts.title: When the six-by-six velocity transform applies
concepts.description: The displayed transform relates two fixed reference frames on the same rigid body; an articulated joint would add relative motion.
concepts.subtopic: When the six-by-six velocity transform applies

concepts.title: Sign of the velocity offset block
concepts.description: Cross-product antisymmetry gives ω×p=−p×ω before the coordinate rotation.

concepts.description: The B-point velocity in A is(1,2,0); rotating by−90° gives(2,−1,0).
